summary: All 10 completed experiments were compute-bound in the locked 74.4-minute window. The 65.33-minute structural-learning task dominated elapsed time, but the available records do not explain its internal cost; the locked compute-task GPU-idle classification is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Measure continuous structural learning on later distinct requests occupied 65.33 of the 74.4 minutes, but the disk-mtime reconstruction has no phase trace that can identify why.
The point-in-time GPU report is not correlated with an experiment execution window, so it cannot establish sustained accelerator efficiency for the compute-bound tasks.
The supplied data has no model-count or runner-selection receipt, so it cannot establish whether any task with two or more models failed to engage DualGPURunner.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-linked monotonic spans for model load, warmup, inference, validation, and artifact writes so the next duration leader has a causal phase breakdown.
Sample device utilization during each active compute window and join every sample to the task, process, and device instead of relying on a closing snapshot.
Record model count, runner choice, and assigned devices at launch; select DualGPURunner only when two or more models are loaded in parallel.
Add restartable checkpoints around the long structural-learning path and place an independent ready model job on the free device when its launch receipt proves that overlap is valid.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add one joined execution receipt with phase spans and task-window GPU telemetry.
Add launch-time model-count, runner-selection, and device-assignment evidence.
Checkpoint the duration-leading path and use eligibility-aware placement for independent compute work.
meta_reflection: The duration ordering identifies where to investigate, not why the work was slow. The closing GPU sample and missing concurrency receipts do not support a sustained-utilization judgment or a DualGPURunner-miss claim.
